note: Adapted from the German genus-level account in Holmgren (1912), who treated Allodontermes as a subgenus of Protermes; Fuller (1921, 1922) treated it as a distinct genus. Alate body length and wing span are taken from Fuller's alate key.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: clypeus largely hyaline; labrum with a hyaline tip; the apical part of the left mandible with 3 small notches on its basal side, the remaining teeth well developed; right mandible with a tooth indication between the middle tooth and the apex; antennae 17-segmented. Alate: medium-sized, body about 10 mm long, wing span about 40 mm, body smooth, yellowish brown, wings hyaline.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head in lateral view, eyes approached; antennae 19-segmented, the 3rd segment shorter than the 2nd and 4th; pronotum about half as long as wide, slightly narrower than the head including the eyes, flat; meso- and metanotum broadly emarginate; fore wing scale distinctly larger than the hind wing scale but not reaching the base of the latter; radius weak, merging early with the anterior wing margin; radial sector reaching the wing apex; media of the fore wing free from the scale, that of the hind wing arising at the base of the radial sector, the media of both wings close to the cubitus; media more or less branched towards the apex.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head relatively large, parallel-sided oval, flatly convex; fontanelle inconspicuous; cranial sutures invisible; basal part of the clypeus rather inflated, transversely oval, fairly large, not quite reaching the mandibular condyles; compound eyes rudimentary or very distinct, even pigmented; mandibular condyles very large; right mandible with an indication of tooth 2; antennae 16–17-segmented, the 2nd longer than the 3rd, the 3rd equal to or slightly longer than the 4th; pronotum small, less than half the head width, its anterior lobe upturned; at least the fore and middle tibiae with lateral spines; fore tibiae with 3 apical spines; styli present.
